chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The injuries of the woman and the man are equal until they reach one-third of the wergild (blood money). So when it exceeds that, the injury of the man is doubled over the injury of the woman by two times.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in blood money for injuries between men and women in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the jurisprudential rule of 'diyah' (blood money), establishing that injuries to men and women are valued equally up to one-third of the full compensation. Beyond this threshold, the man's injury compensation is doubled relative to the woman's, a distinction rooted in classical Shia fiqh that reflects the historical context of male financial responsibility for the family. This ruling highlights the nuanced application of equity versus equality in Islamic inheritance and compensation laws.
